definitions.meaning: something that happens unexpectedly, without warning, comes from nowhere
taken literally, the phrase describes falling ... heavens

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about something abruptly falling from the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means unexpectedly; read literally it is falling from the azure heavens.

clue.text: Where fruit grows, or variety of beet

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable that is a cultivated form of beet

explanation.surface: A gardener's choice between a fruit plot and a kind of beetroot.
explanation.definitionFit: An enclosed plot planted with fruit trees is the place where apples and pears are grown.

clue.text: Crown, one stolen by a knave, turned over

indicators.note: turned over means the assembled letters are read in reverse, as this is a down clue flipped
the letter for one is taken in, held inside, by the rogue

parts.note: a knave is a rogue, and a rat is a treacherous scoundrel
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A tale of a jewelled crown pinched by a rogue and turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stolen by' puts I inside A RAT to give ARAIT; 'turned over' then reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled headband worn by royalty or nobility is a kind of crown or coronet.

parts.note: flash means showy or ostentatious
in football or rugby, a back is a defensive player

explanation.surface: A recollection of a showy footballer who played in defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinema technique showing an earlier scene, often a character's recollection of the past.

clue.text: African shelter on base of plateau

parts.note: a hut is a simple shelter

indicators.note: in a down clue the base of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A shack in Africa built at the foot of a high plateau.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a Bantu people living mainly in Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa.

clue.text: Far from excited about line taken temporarily

indicators.note: about means going around, so the uninterested word wraps the line

parts.note: bored is the opposite of excited
a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: Someone unmoved by a line they have only on loan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far from excited' is a roundabout way of saying uninterested; 'about' signals wrapping round the line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on loan, to be given back later, has been taken for a time only.

parts.note: a side that is up is ahead, winning
a set is a series or collection, as in tennis a set of games

explanation.surface: A sports report on an unexpected outcome in a run of matches.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport an underdog beating the favourite is called this: an unexpected outcome.

clue.text: Where one waits to see North African volcano from below

indicators.note: in a down clue, reading from below means the letters run upwards, backwards

parts.note: a Moor is a member of a Muslim people of north-west Africa
Etna is the volcano on Sicily

explanation.surface: A traveller waiting to view an African volcano from its foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room leading into a larger one, often used as a waiting area.

indicators.note: stuffed suggests the letters are crammed and jumbled together

explanation.surface: An absurd picture of food crammed into someone's ears.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a sandwich, a light bite eaten between meals.

definitions.meaning: an eccentric, entertaining person is called a real one of these
a written symbol such as a letter of an alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone's funny letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertaining, eccentric person is a 'real character'; a written symbol is also one.

clue.text: Seasonal visitor, hill-dweller in South Africa

indicators.note: in says the insect goes inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: an ant lives in an anthill

explanation.surface: A seasonal guest who lives in the hills of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas visits once a year at Christmas, bringing presents.

clue.text: Lack of concern with route passing through outskirts of Aylesbury

indicators.note: the route goes through, so sits inside, the outer letters
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: a path is a route

explanation.surface: Indifference to a road running through the edge of Aylesbury, a Buckinghamshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Indifference, an absence of interest or feeling, is a lack of concern.

clue.text: Ten hours travelling in one direction

indicators.note: travelling says the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: A long ten-hour journey heading one way.
explanation.definitionFit: Toward the south is one point of the compass, hence a single heading.

indicators.note: in says the doctrine goes inside the period

parts.note: a day is a period of time
an ism is a doctrine or ideology

explanation.surface: Anxiety caused by a creed of the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Consternation and alarm are a state of perturbation.

parts.note: a spruce is a conifer typically used as a Christmas tree
something erected is put up

explanation.surface: Smartening a Christmas tree once it has been put up.
explanation.definitionFit: To smarten or neaten is the phrasal verb for tidying a place or oneself.

clue.text: Ruby, perhaps unexpectedly, gets on with me

indicators.note: unexpectedly signals the letters turn up in a surprising order

explanation.surface: Ruby, a woman, surprisingly gets along with the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruby looks like a woman's name; it is an example of a precious stone.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruby is one example of a precious stone, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Best people in chant making a lot of noise

indicators.note: in says the elite go inside the chanting

parts.note: to sing is to chant
the cream is the best of a group

explanation.surface: The elite chanting loudly at an event.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrieking or yelling loudly is making a great deal of noise.

definitions.meaning: a short quip delivered in a single sentence
whimsically, a railway on a single track is a vehicle running on one rail

explanation.surface: A quip about a single-rail train.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief quip in a single sentence; whimsically, a train running on just one rail.

definitions.meaning: workers withdrawing their labour in a dispute are on strike

explanation.surface: A notable walkout by workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Means both conspicuous and impressive, and taking industrial action by downing tools.

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting part goes underneath the street

parts.note: ripe means ready, as fruit to be eaten

explanation.surface: A band ready to back a street event.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow line of colour is a band, as on a flag.

clue.text: Illegal act on a European peninsula

parts.note: a crime is an illegal act

explanation.surface: Something unlawful happening on a European peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: A large peninsula jutting into the Black Sea, part of eastern Europe.

indicators.note: gathered suggests letters collected up and put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An actor resting, so the speaker understood.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional performer, such as a singer or dancer, is a player on stage.

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters are in a terrible state, so reorganised

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict that the shows were plainly dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerts given by a solo musician or small group are performances.

definitions.meaning: lifting is slang for shoplifting, an act of stealing
split as two words, it is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A question about a newspaper and some lifting.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as THE FT, it names the Financial Times, a British daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the act of lifting; split it is the Financial Times newspaper.

definitions.meaning: to end up or turn out in a certain way
whimsically, a frying pan taken out of the cupboard for cooking

explanation.surface: Wrapping things up once the meal is ready to be prepared.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means turn out or end up; literally, a cooking vessel that has been got out.

parts.note: mega means great or excellent

explanation.surface: A grand old letter from Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet, used by Athenians.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Spanish princess's favourite drink is a type of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkling white Italian wine from Piedmont.

definitions.meaning: to trim or lop branches from a plant
a dried plum is also slang for a foolish person

explanation.surface: An idiot being chopped away.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim branches is to lop them off; the dried plum is also slang for a fool.

clue.text: Unpleasant behaviour as tennis star's beginning to flip

indicators.note: to flip means to go wild, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tennis star throwing a tantrum on court.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite and meanness of conduct are unpleasant behaviour.

clue.text: Everyone attending event after jumping barrier on racecourse

indicators.note: after says the attendance figure comes later than the jumping

parts.note: starting means jumping with surprise
the gate is the number of spectators attending a sports event

explanation.surface: Racegoers arrive after a horse clears a barrier at the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gate' is the British term for a match's attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: The barrier from which horses are released to begin a race.
